answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 13 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, which means paying the sparrow bond on all of them and exposing each to the plume slash. Because the sonnet audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A farm of 257 pays that 128 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
